_comment: NVTX annotations for nsys --python-functions-trace, so the timeline
names the Python function that issued each CUDA row.
Needs the nvtx package in the target interpreter. Module names must
include parent packages, and methods are written Class.method.
Read the result with, in increasing specificity:
nsys stats --report nvtx_sum       <rep>   time per range
nsys stats --report nvtx_kern_sum  <rep>   kernel time per range
nsys stats --report nvtx_gpu_proj_trace <rep>   each GPU op to its range
Prefer this over --python-sampling: on nsys 2025.6.3 that flag
produced no Python backtraces at all here, silently.
CPU preprocessing: the weight cache and the coordinate crop.
These nest, and both halves are listed on purpose.
cache:  DynamicFeature.cache = Feature.cache (shared topology scan)
+ cache_properties. Annotating only Feature.cache showed about a
third of the real cost.
query:  DensityFlow/MarchingObservers.query are thin shims that call
super().query, so the work sits in DynamicFeature.query.
The CUDA boundary. _dispatch_grid launches and returns a collector,
so its range is the launch only -- the wait shows up wherever the
collector is called, inside _run_prepared_tasks.
Synchronous entry points, used by custom features.
Trajectory IO, the other big host cost.
pytraj. Only module-level plain-Python functions can be wrapped.
Do NOT list pytraj.Trajectory or pytraj.Topology: those are classes,
and replacing them with a function wrapper breaks isinstance and
nearl.io.traj.Trajectory's subclassing of them.
Topology.select is unreachable this way -- it is a
cython_function_or_method on an immutable extension type, so setattr
is refused. Its cost shows up inside Feature.cache and
Featurizer.parse_focus, which do bracket it.
Where the pt.load actually happens on the pipeline path.
Setup path, to account for the gap between the first pytraj.load and
Featurizer.run. The profiler's own build_featurizer cannot be annotated:
it runs as __main__, and nsys resolves modules by importable name.
